original_question: Let f (x) ∈ Z[x] be a polynomial of degree at least 2, and let α ∈ Z be a wandering point for f . Then Of (α) contains only finitely many primes. More generally, let K be a number field. For each prime ideal p of the ring ordp : K ։ Z be the associated normalized valuation, and ∗ of integers of K, let + let ordp (α) = max ordp (α), 0 . Then we have the following natural generalization of Conjecture 20.2.
target_in_paper: Section 20, Conjecture 20.3, the natural generalization of Conjecture 20.2 about bounded total positive valuations of the orbit differences f^n(α)-β over a number field.
correct_elements: The draft correctly reproduces Conjecture 20.2 and then correctly begins the setup for its official generalization in the paper: it switches to a number field K, introduces prime ideals of the ring of integers of K, uses the normalized valuation ord_p, and defines ord_p^+(x)=max{ord_p(x),0}. That matches exactly the lead-in sentence immediately preceding Conjecture 20.3 in Section 20.
missing_details: The draft stops before the actual statement of Conjecture 20.3, namely the finiteness of the set {n ≥ 0 : Σ_p ord_p^+(f^n(α)-β) ≤ c}.
It does not state that f is now a rational function f(x) ∈ K(x), not a polynomial in Z[x].
It omits the degree restriction in the generalized statement: deg(f) ≥ 2.
It omits the variables β ∈ K and the fixed constant c.
It does not say that the sum is taken over all prime ideals p of the ring of integers O_K of K.
It does not define the orbit notation O_f(α)={f^n(α): n ≥ 0}.
It does not define 'wandering' in the paper’s sense, namely that O_f(α) is infinite.

It leaves implicit that ord_p is defined on K^*; if f^n(α)=β for some n, that exceptional case is not addressed in the draft. Since α is wandering, this can happen at most once, so it does not affect the finiteness assertion, but a stand-alone question should acknowledge the nonzero-input issue.
It refers to 'the following natural generalization of Conjecture 20.2' without actually stating that generalization, so it is not stand-alone.
It does not specify that K is a number field in the paper’s sense, i.e. a finite extension of Q, although this is part of the paper’s background notation.
refined_question: Let K be a number field with ring of integers O_K. For each prime ideal p of O_K, let ord_p: K^* → Z be the normalized valuation, and define ord_p^+(x):=max{ord_p(x),0}. Let f(x) ∈ K(x) be a rational function of degree at least 2, let α ∈ K be a wandering point for f (so O_f(α)={f^n(α): n ≥ 0} is infinite), let β ∈ K, and fix a constant c ∈ R. Is the set of integers n ≥ 0 such that Σ_p ord_p^+(f^n(α)-β) ≤ c finite, where the sum runs over all prime ideals p of O_K?
justification: The draft is aiming at Conjecture 20.3, not merely Conjecture 20.2. The reason is that it first gives the exact text of Conjecture 20.2 and then immediately continues with the exact introductory sentence that the paper uses to introduce Conjecture 20.3 ('More generally ... Then we have the following natural generalization of Conjecture 20.2'), but it stops before the actual generalized finiteness statement. The needed notation for the forward orbit O_f(α) and the paper’s definition of 'wandering' comes from Definition 2.1 in Section 2, while 'number field' is fixed in Section 3. Remark 20.1 supplies the heuristic motivation for why the authors expect only very few primes in an orbit, and Conjectures 20.2 and 20.3 are then stated consecutively in Section 20. The paper does not give an explicit equivalent reformulation of Conjecture 20.3 nearby, so no alternate formulation should be added.
